subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: For WebChat backed by Codex native threads, should `chat.send` keep immediate `started` semantics, or must it fail fast until a runnable Codex thread/turn is proven?
rationale: The code can be repaired several ways, but choosing between API semantics, force-rotation, delayed ACK, health/audit surfacing, and doctor recovery changes the user-visible contract.

options.title: Fail fast or rotate before ACK
options.body: Require the Gateway to prove or create a runnable Codex thread before returning `started`, surfacing a visible error when recovery is impossible.

options.title: Keep ACK semantics with recovery telemetry
options.body: Keep immediate `started`, but add watchdog, tasks audit, and user-visible recovery when no dispatch or Codex turn begins promptly.

options.title: Wait for live repro first
options.body: Hold implementation until a packaged fixture or live replay of the reported persisted native-thread state confirms the exact current-main failure.

recommendation.title: Fail fast or rotate before ACK
recommendation.body: Require the Gateway to prove or create a runnable Codex thread before returning `started`, surfacing a visible error when recovery is impossible.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the most recent merged native-thread overflow mitigation that would shape the next contract decision.
